notesStmt.note: This manuscript was likely composed in late 1884 or 1885.

A draft of "You Tides With Ceaseless Swell," one of eight poems in the "Fancies at Navesink" sequence, which first appeared in print in the August 1885 issue of Nineteenth Century. The sequence was later reprinted in November Boughs (1888).

and ebb.
lg.l:
You ? ocean tides with ceaseless swell! and you
ebb! you power that does this work!

You unseen force, centripetal, centrif-
ugalcentrifugal
, through space's spread! entire!

You intermutual chain‸Rapport of sun, moon,
earth, and all the constellations!

What are the messages by you from
distant stars to us? what Sirius'?
what Capella's?

What central heart—and you the pulse—
vivifies all? What boundless ag-
gregateaggregate
of all?

What subtle indirection and significance
in you? what clue to all in you?
what fluid vast identity

Holding the universe ‸with all its parts entire as one—as sailing
in a ship?
